svg.aria-label: Sequence diagram of one node: boot with a fresh id and create its registration; heartbeat every 10 seconds with If-Match; on stop keep heartbeating until the in-flight requests end, then exit; if it goes silent the leader treats it as departed after 60 seconds and reaps the entries it held; after ten times that and with no entry naming it, the leader deletes the registration.
svg.title: One node: boot, heartbeat, stop or silence, and how the leader forgets it
svg.text: One node: boot, heartbeat, stop or silence, and how the leader forgets it
A node
Hot tier
Leader
1 boot: a fresh id <node>-<boot id>, never reused
create _tiering/proxies/<id>, create-only: {proto, boot, hb}
2 every 10 s: rewrite the registration, If-Match
live_until = send time of the last good heartbeat + D - m
serves requests; each put or delete
holds an entry named with its id
Stop: graceful
3 drain: stop accepting, keep heartbeating until
in-flight requests have finished (a cap cuts long ones)
4 exit. There is no closed flag: the registration
just goes quiet, as after a crash
Silence: crash, kill or freeze (and the end of a graceful stop)
5 scan: registration unchanged for D = 60 s on the leader's
own monotonic clock since it first saw that exact object: departed
6 every HELD entry of that id: CAS to PENDING (reap); finish it
7 after 10 D, with no entry naming the id: delete the registration
No timestamp from another machine is compared with anything. A restarted process has a new id, so it is never mistaken for its dead predecessor.
The old per-node journals, checkpoints, prune and sentinels are not part of this: a node leaves nothing to rebuild but its entries.
